newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ITC says excise duty almost paid.
newsitem.headline: India's ITC says excise duty almost paid.

text.p: Indian tobacco and hotels company ITC Ltd said on Monday that by the end of September it had paid 3.2 billion rupees in owed excise duty out of 3.5 billion which must be paid to the government by next year.

The Central Excise Gold and Appellate Tribunal (CEGAT) ordered ITC in March to pay 3.5 billion rupees in excise duty for the period between March 1983 and February 1987. The payment is due by January 1, 1997.
In late March, ITC said it had paid 1.7 billion rupees in owed excise duty.

ITC said in a statement accompanying its results for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) that by September 30, it had deposited 3.2 billion rupees, including 900 million covering instalments for the months of October, November and December 1996, paid in advance.
"The referred CEGAT order will be fully complied with by the due date," it said.
Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc is the biggest single shareholder in ITC with a 31.7 percent stake.
